title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: A Short-Notice Initial Declaration in a Decided File
content:
## Principle

The account of a Dangerous Goods Acceptance file on which a review decision is given must also agree with the notice the shipper actually gave. Where the signed initial declaration came in with too little notice, the file carries a late declaration fee, and a decision can be given only on an account showing a late declaration fee entry that refers to that signed initial declaration. The charge is one that a decided file can no longer take, so a decided file with a short-notice declaration and no such entry is not a state the product provides for. A file in which the entry is missing therefore stays under review, and no decision is entered on it.

## What counts as too little notice

- **Signing date:** the date part of the moment the signed initial declaration was registered in the declaration file; where more than one is signed, the one registered last.
- **Notice given:** the calendar days from that signing date to the ETD shown on the booking carrying the goods.
- **Too little:** fewer days than the category's required lead time.
- **No charge in question:** a declaration whose notice meets the required lead time, and any acceptance whose booking shows no scheduled departure.

## Worked cases (invented required lead time of 8 days)

| Signing date | ETD on the booking | Days of notice | Late fee entry naming the declaration | Decision possible on this ground |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-02-02 | 2026-02-12 | 10 | none | yes |
| 2026-02-02 | 2026-02-10 | 8 | none | yes |
| 2026-02-02 | 2026-02-08 | 6 | none | no |
| 2026-02-02 | 2026-02-08 | 6 | present | yes |
| 2026-02-02 | no ETD shown | — | none | yes |
